text:
Diego: Hey everyone, day 3 here. Using Ubuntu 22.04 on a work machine. Trying to get asdf to manage ruby/node/go, but I'm hitting PATH/shim issues and git keeps using system ruby gems. Also my SSH keys don't forward into tmux sessions. Anyone done the Linux bootstrap recently?
Ana: welcome! :wave: common checklist: install build-essential, libssl-dev, zlib1g-dev, and make sure asdf is in ~/.bashrc or ~/.profile depending on login shell. What shell are you using?
Diego: bash, but I use GNOME Terminal and also start tmux from a desktop shortcut. I added `source ~/.asdf/asdf.sh` to ~/.bashrc. `asdf list` shows plugins but `ruby -v` reports system 2.7.
Riley: check `which ruby` and `asdf which ruby`. If `which ruby` points to /usr/bin, your shell login vs non-login init mismatch is likely. Put asdf init in ~/.profile or ~/.bash_profile so GUI terminals inherit it. For bash add: `echo -e '\n. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh' >> ~/.profile` then log out.
Diego: ok changed to ~/.profile and reloaded; `ruby -v` now picks up asdf shim but `gem install bundler` still tries to write to /usr/lib and fails with permission denied.
Ana: install ruby with `RUBY_CONFIGURE_OPTS=--with-jemalloc asdf install ruby 3.1.2` (example) and avoid `sudo gem install`. Ensure `gem` uses your home dir by setting `export GEM_HOME=$HOME/.gem` and adding `$GEM_HOME/bin` to PATH. Also consider `--user-install`.
Diego: that fixed gems. Node is odd: npm global packages go to /usr/local even though asdf Node is active. `npm root -g` -> /usr/local/lib/node_modules.
Riley: set npm prefix to your home: `mkdir -p ~/.npm-global && npm config set prefix '~/.npm-global'` and add `~/.npm-global/bin` to PATH. Or reinstall node with asdf after ensuring no stale /usr/local node binaries: `sudo rm /usr/local/bin/node` if that's safe.
Diego: removed old node binary; now node and npm globals are local. Thanks. SSH/tmux problem: when I ssh to a server and start tmux, my forwarded agent stops working inside tmux. `ssh -A` used.
Sam: tmux can inherit a stale SSH_AUTH_SOCK if tmux started before agent. Use `update-environment` in tmux.conf or run `tmux set-environment -g SSH_AUTH_SOCK $SSH_AUTH_SOCK` after connecting, or use a socket proxy like `socat` approach. Example in ~/.tmux.conf:
```
set-option -g update-environment "SSH_AUTH_SOCK"
```
Then after attaching a session, run `tmux show-environment -s` to verify.
Diego: adding update-environment worked! Keys are available in tmux now. One last minor thing: my dotfiles symlink script overwrote my .bashrc with a file that expects zsh. Now my GNOME terminal launches a blank shell. :sweat_smile:
Ana: always run the dotfile installer in dry-run mode first. Check the dotfiles repo README for `install.sh --check` or `stow -n`. Restore from backup or check the repo's branch `legacy/bash` for bash-friendly config.
Diego: restored bashrc from backup and ran stow properly. All green: asdf-managed ruby/node/go, npm/gems in home, ssh agent in tmux. Huge thanks! :tada:
DevEx Bot: Congrats Diego! If you'd like the one-liner bootstrap, run: `curl -fsSL https://get.redwood.dev/bootstrap | bash` (inspects for Linux). Internal docs: https://intranet.redwood/company/onboarding/dev-setup and dotfiles: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dotfiles. Ping #devex for pairing on any stubborn env issues.
